Record each missing, ambiguous or unsupported field by source row. 3. If any row fails this gate, do not calculate or present a full-list mass total. Preserve unresolved rows with explicit unknown fields and no invented mass. methods.title: Row-preserving small inventory quantity and mass reconciliation

data.applicability: Small readable item lists with quantities and per-item masses in mg or g, including incomplete and mixed-unit fictional training lists. Incomplete lists permit only a validated partial subtotal, never a full mass total. Repeated item codes do not identify duplicate rows.
data.instructions: 1. Read the complete retained input text and extraction warnings. Establish explicit field meanings. Assign every source data row a stable ordinal; preserve its code, order, quantity, original per-item mass value and original unit. Never merge or discard repeated codes. Distinguish headers and blanks from data. 2. Mandatory gate BEFORE any arithmetic: inspect EVERY source row and establish whether its per-piece mass AND explicit unit are known. Also validate quantity as an unambiguous nonnegative integer, mass as an unambiguous nonnegative decimal and unit as mg or g. Do not infer a unit or mass from neighboring rows. Record each missing, ambiguous or unsupported field by source row. 3. If any row fails this gate, do not calculate or present a full-list mass total. Calculate only rows whose required fields are explicitly validated; label their sum CONFIRMED PARTIAL SUBTOTAL and state its row coverage and exclusions. List all missing or unresolved data by row and ask for clarification. Never treat an excluded row as zero, silently repair it, or extrapolate. If no row qualifies, report that no confirmed mass subtotal is available. A separately known quantity count must not be presented as complete mass coverage. 4. For validated rows normalize per-item mass to grams: mg / 1000; g unchanged. Retain original value and unit alongside the normalized value. Use exact integer or decimal arithmetic without rounding. Compute row mass as quantity times normalized per-item grams. A full total is allowed only when EVERY source row passes the gate. 5. Independently verify row count and ordered identifiers against the complete source, every included conversion and product, and sums through an independent route such as integer milligrams with repeated addition compared to decimal grams. Execute an ordinary calculation tool when available and retain its actual observation. Reprinting the same total is not independent verification. Partial-subtotal verification does not verify unknown rows or a full mass total. 6. Produce an ordered table with source row ordinal, code, quantity, ORIGINAL per-item mass value and unit, normalized per-item mass in g, and row mass in g. Preserve unresolved rows with explicit unknown fields and no invented mass. Give coverage, quantity counts clearly distinguished from mass coverage, and either a checked full total or ONLY the confirmed partial subtotal with missing-data list. Document checks, unresolved issues, assumptions and rounding. Optional kg cannot replace grams. 7. Retain full result and exact input and Method version in a Run/invocation. Separate model application reports, observed arithmetic checks and user usefulness. Never rewrite historical results or old invocations when revising this general method. A Method correction is not a new calculation, verification, demonstrated improvement or resolution of a missing-data problem.
data.input_contract: Readable source list with row quantities, per-item mass values and explicit mg or g units. Incomplete fields are accepted only for preflight identification and validated partial reporting; complete full-total calculation requires all rows to pass. Paths and output language are invocation bindings.

Independent checks cover only validated data.

data.applicability: Small readable item lists with quantities and per-item masses in mg or g, including incomplete and mixed-unit fictional training lists. Incomplete lists permit only a validated partial subtotal, never a full mass total. Repeated item codes do not identify duplicate rows.
data.instructions: 1. Read the complete retained input text and extraction warnings. Establish explicit field meanings. Assign every source data row a stable ordinal; preserve its code, order, quantity, original per-item mass value and original unit. Never merge or discard repeated codes. Distinguish headers and blanks from data. 2. Mandatory gate BEFORE any arithmetic: inspect EVERY source row and establish whether its per-piece mass AND explicit unit are known. Also validate quantity as an unambiguous nonnegative integer, mass as an unambiguous nonnegative decimal and unit as mg or g. Do not infer a unit or mass from neighboring rows. Record each missing, ambiguous or unsupported field by source row. 3. If any row fails this gate, do not calculate or present a full-list mass total. Calculate only rows whose required fields are explicitly validated; label their sum CONFIRMED PARTIAL SUBTOTAL and state its row coverage and exclusions. List all missing or unresolved data by row and ask for clarification. Never treat an excluded row as zero, silently repair it, or extrapolate. If no row qualifies, report that no confirmed mass subtotal is available. A separately known quantity count must not be presented as complete mass coverage. 4. For validated rows normalize per-item mass to grams: mg / 1000; g unchanged. Retain original value and unit alongside the normalized value. Use exact integer or decimal arithmetic without rounding. Compute row mass as quantity times normalized per-item grams. A full total is allowed only when EVERY source row passes the gate. 5. Independently verify row count and ordered identifiers against the complete source, every included conversion and product, and sums through an independent route such as integer milligrams with repeated addition compared to decimal grams. Execute an ordinary calculation tool when available and retain its actual observation. Reprinting the same total is not independent verification. Partial-subtotal verification does not verify unknown rows or a full mass total. 6. Produce an ordered table with source row ordinal, code, quantity, ORIGINAL per-item mass value and unit, normalized per-item mass in g, and row mass in g. Preserve unresolved rows with explicit unknown fields and no invented mass. Give coverage, quantity counts clearly distinguished from mass coverage, and either a checked full total or ONLY the confirmed partial subtotal with missing-data list. Document checks, unresolved issues, assumptions and rounding. Optional kg cannot replace grams. 7. Retain full result and exact input and Method version in a Run/invocation.
